candidate_prompt.title: First Repeating Element
candidate_prompt.statement: Given an array of integers nums, find the first element that repeats in the array. If no element repeats, return None. An element is considered repeating if it appears more than once and its second occurrence has the smallest index.

approach_criteria.description: Uses a hash set to track seen elements in one pass
approach_criteria.interviewer_probe: That sounds like a solid O(n) approach. How will you keep track of which element appeared first versus second occurrence?

approach_criteria.description: Sorts the array to find duplicates adjacent to each other
approach_criteria.interviewer_probe: Sorting can group duplicates, but what happens to the original element indices and ordering when you sort?
That will find duplicates, but what would the time complexity be for an array with 100,000 elements?

common_misconceptions.description: Claimed O(1) space while allocating a hash set that stores up to N distinct elements.
Assumed hash set lookups take O(n) instead of average O(1).

follow_ups.prompt: What if the input stream is potentially infinite and you have bounded memory? How could you approximate or handle the stream?
What if we also need to return the tuple of exact 0-based indices (first_index, second_index) of the duplicate?
